Dangriga (Belize)

Also find this entry through: Dangriga

Dangriga’s local Garifuna history can be approached through civic memory, cultural education and the work of the Gulisi Museum. A community-authored primer and dated interviews offer starting perspectives without making the entire town or its institutions interchangeable with one people.

Read the sources [1] I. Myrtle Palacio; digital edition hosted by NICH [2] News5 Belize

01

Civic memory and recognition

In her 2024 primer, I. Myrtle Palacio connects Garifuna civic participation with Dangriga. Her selected discussion recalls assistance to 1931 hurricane refugees and names C.J. Benguche, T.V. Ramos and Mateo Avaloy in the movement for a public day of recognition. It is an authored historical interpretation; the underlying records and wider political history remain further research.

Read the sources [1] I. Myrtle Palacio; digital edition hosted by NICH

02

A museum built to tell a story

News5’s November 2004 opening report records National Garifuna Council president Michael Polonio’s emphasis on passing ancestral stories to children. NICH representative Yasser Musa describes contributions to the exhibits by Joseph Palacio and Sebastian Cayetano. The report gives readers named voices in public history; it does not turn every reported ancestral story into a verified genealogy.

Read the sources [2] News5 Belize

03

Preservation is continuing work

A separate 2019 report covers an agreement to rehabilitate the Gulisi Museum. Interviewees explain why exhibits should help residents and visitors understand Garifuna history. The announcement documents intentions and partnerships at that time; it does not establish that every refurbishment was completed or describe current opening arrangements.

Read the sources [3] News5 Belize

The First Primer on the People Called Garifuna — selected civic-history pages ↗

Publication: 2024 edition

I. Myrtle Palacio’s 2024 edition connects Garifuna civic participation with Dangriga and the movement for public recognition. This selected account is useful beside dated museum interviews and further archival work.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Actual root-cached NICH-hosted PDF, selected PDFpp.25–27 (printed19–21), read for civic advocacy, the Dangriga 1931-refugee reference and recognition-day advocates. Duplicate extraction passages treated as the same text.

Review recorded: October 29, 2026

Access note: Not all50pages or underlying statutes, election records, precise voter outcomes, political totals or restricted spiritual chapter reviewed. No current legal determination. This is the author’s account, not government authorship or a licence for images/maps.

New Garifuna museum opens in Dangriga ↗

Publication: 2004-11-18

The November18,2004 opening report records National Garifuna Council and NICH voices about building the Gulisi Museum, shaping exhibits and sharing ancestral stories. Keep their interpretations attributed.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Actual full main report and quoted interviews read from normal HTTP 200 HTML; Janelle Chanona reporting, Michael Polonio and Yasser Musa interviews. Unrelated archive navigation/comments not reviewed as sources.

Review recorded: October 29, 2026

Access note: Dated opening report, not current hours, present leadership, visitor numbers or independent confirmation of every genealogical/ancestral statement. Underlying interviews beyond the transcript and museum objects/media not inspected or reproduced.

Rehabilitating the Gulisi Garifuna Museum ↗

Publication: 2019-08-06

The August6,2019 report records a rehabilitation agreement and interviews with NICH, funder and National Garifuna Council representatives about telling Garifuna history. An announced project is not evidence that all proposed work was completed.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Actual complete main report and interviews read from normal HTTP 200 HTML, including Janelle Carcamo, Sapna Budhrani, John August Jr. and Sandra Miranda statements.

Review recorded: October 29, 2026

Access note: Agreement, funding and intended exhibits are reported in 2019; current officeholders, later completion, impact and public access are not inferred. No underlying grant files, original broadcasts or museum media examined.
